result.title: SurgWorld: Learning Surgical Representations Beyond Observation via Latent Prediction
result.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
result.summary: Surgical procedures are inherently partially observable, requiring surgeons to continuously infer evolving anatomical dynamics and future surgical states beyond the current observation. However, existing self-supervised learning methods primarily learn from observed surgical videos through masked reconstruction or predicting representations within the camera's current field of view, lacking the capability to explicitly model the out-of-sight surgical dynamics. Inspired by latent predictive world models, we introduce SurgWorld, a video-native, self-supervised framework for surgical representation learning, which treats a specified spatial or temporal shift as a pseudo-action and learns to predict the target latent representation from a partial observation. Specifically, we propose Out-of-Sight Dynamics Modeling (OSDM) as the pretraining objective for predicting representations conditioned on relative spatio-temporal shifts. We further regularize the learned latent dynamics from OSDM with a Geometric Visual Similarity (GVS) objective by aligning patch-level relational structures between predicted and target representations, preserving spatial geometry and local visual coherence for dense perception. These two objectives are integrated through an agglomerative training framework that consolidates complementary supervisory signals from multiple teachers to learn a unified latent representation of surgical dynamics and visual geometry. Extensive transfer learning experiments on 17 surgical benchmarks show that SurgWorld consistently outperforms existing vision foundation models across surgical workflow recognition, fine-grained action understanding, and dense visual perception. We further conduct tailored qualitative and quantitative analyses, demonstrating that SurgWorld effectively captures surgical dynamics beyond the directly observed context through latent prediction.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SurgWorld 手术视频自监督表征框架：把空间或时间偏移视为伪动作，从部分观测预测目标的 latent 表示（OSDM），并用 patch 级几何视觉相似度（GVS）对齐预测与目标表示的关系结构，在多教师聚合训练下于 17 个手术基准做迁移评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以偏移为条件预测 latent 状态」与 patch 级关系结构对齐，可能为 LVR 的状态更新监督和 latent 相似度的位置/结构度量提供核查线索，但属手术视频表征预训练，未涉及推理期 latent 生成或答案使用。
